CXR: bilateral lobar consolidation (right > left). Sputum culture: Streptococcus pneumoniae (pending sensitivities). Antibiotics: amoxicillin-clavulanate 1.2g TDS + clarithromycin 500mg BD IV. Physiotherapy: airway clearance BD. Glucose management ongoing (stress hyperglycaemia). Renal function and electrolytes normal. No active bleeding.

treatment: Post-operative care: Emergency laparotomy for perforated peptic ulcer
note_text: Post-operative day 0. Emergency laparotomy 4 hours ago for perforated peptic ulcer with generalised peritonitis. Graham patch repair performed, peritoneal washout x4 litres. Currently intubated (deep sedation: propofol + fentanyl infusion). NG tube in situ, free drainage. Right-sided drain output 120 ml/hr serosanguineous. Antibiotics: cefuroxime 1.5g TDS + metronidazole 500mg TDS. FBC: Hb 91, WBC 18.6, Plt 312. Lactate 2.4 mmol/L. Plan: ICU overnight, aim for extubation tomorrow if cardiovascularly stable.

treatment: Hypertensive emergency with acute hypertensive encephalopathy (PRES confirmed on CT)
note_text: Hypertensive emergency: BP 230/140 mmHg on arrival with confusion, severe occipital headache, visual disturbance (blurred vision, photopsia) and vomiting. CT head: no haemorrhage, bilateral posterior white matter T2 signal change (PRES pattern). Fundoscopy: papilloedema grade 3, flame-shaped haemorrhages. IV labetalol infusion commenced (current rate 4 mg/min): BP now 185/110 and decreasing. Target: reduce MAP by 20-25% over first hour, then gradually to 160/100 over 24h. Creatinine 145 umol/L (possible hypertensive nephrosclerosis). Ophthalmic review. Secondary causes workup: renal artery Doppler, aldosterone:renin ratio, catecholamines.

Haemodynamically unstable on arrival: BP 82/50, HR 128, SpO2 88% on 15L non-rebreathe. Decision for systemic thrombolysis: alteplase 100mg over 2 hours administered. Post-thrombolysis (current): BP 95/62, HR 112, SpO2 96% on 6L/min. Anticoagulation: unfractionated heparin infusion commenced 2h post-thrombolysis. Repeat echo at 6h. Monitor closely for haemorrhagic complications.

note_text: Multi-organ failure: cardiogenic shock (EF 15% on TTE), AKI stage 3 (creatinine 620 umol/L), transaminitis (ALT 892, AST 1024). IABP in situ (1:1 counterpulsation). Cardiology: considering ECMO if haemodynamics deteriorate. Full metabolic workup pending. Prognosis discussed with family.

treatment: Post-operative care: Orthotopic liver transplantation for end-stage liver disease (MELD 28)
note_text: Post-operative day 1 following orthotopic liver transplantation for alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD score 28, donor-recipient match excellent). Bile T-tube output 80 ml/hr (golden bile - primary graft function). LFTs improving: ALT 240 (was 890 POD0), bilirubin 85 (was 148). Immunosuppression: tacrolimus (FK506) target trough 10-15 ng/ml + mycophenolate mofetil 750mg BD. CMV prophylaxis: valganciclovir. PJP prophylaxis: co-trimoxazole. Extubated this morning, SpO2 97% on 4L/min. Epidural analgesia providing good pain control.

treatment: Massive upper GI haemorrhage - bleeding peptic ulcer (Forrest Ia), post-endoscopic haemostasis
note_text: Massive upper GI haemorrhage. Emergency OGD: Forrest Ia bleeding peptic ulcer (posterior wall duodenum, 2cm diameter). Dual endoscopic therapy: 1:10,000 adrenaline injection + haemoclip application - haemostasis achieved. Pre-endoscopy: Hb 61 g/L, BP 88/54. Resuscitation: 2 units pRBC transfused intra-procedure (Hb now 82 g/L). High-dose IV PPI: omeprazole 80mg bolus then 8mg/hr infusion. NBM. Repeat OGD planned at 24 hours. Surgical and interventional radiology team on standby. H. pylori CLO test taken during endoscopy.

treatment: Post-operative care: Right lower lobectomy for stage II non-small-cell lung cancer
note_text: Post right lower lobectomy for stage IIA non-small-cell lung cancer (adenocarcinoma, T2bN0M0). Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) approach. Epidural analgesia (bupivacaine 0.1% + fentanyl 2 mcg/ml at 8 ml/hr) providing excellent pain control (NRS 3/10 on movement). Chest drains x2: air leak resolved at 2h post-op, current output 45 ml/hr serosanguineous. SpO2 97% on 4L/min O2 via nasal cannula. CXR: right lower zone atelectasis - physiotherapy twice daily. Deep breathing exercises. Early mobilisation: sat out of bed at 6h post-op. Surgical oncology follow-up in 4 weeks.

Chest drains x2: air leak resolved at 2h post-op, current output 45 ml/hr serosanguineous. SpO2 97% on 4L/min O2 via nasal cannula. CXR: right lower zone atelectasis - physiotherapy twice daily. Deep breathing exercises. Early mobilisation: sat out of bed at 6h post-op. Surgical oncology follow-up in 4 weeks.

treatment: Severe acute pancreatitis with 60% pancreatic necrosis
note_text: Severe acute pancreatitis (Ranson score 5, APACHE II 18). CT abdomen (CECT): 60% pancreatic necrosis (Balthazar grade E). Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation: Hartmann's 250 ml/hr (total 4200 ml last 16h). Nil by mouth. TPN commenced (2000 kcal, 1.5g protein/kg/day). Analgesia: morphine PCA 1mg bolus + paracetamol 1g q6h. WBC 18.2, CRP 312, lipase 2840 U/L. Surgical review: conservative management initially. Antibiotics withheld unless infection confirmed. ERCP considered if common bile duct calculi on MRCP.
